extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys, agents, applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for examination of U.S. patent applications including inventorship/derivation affidavits, prior art disqualification, file-wrapper handling, search documentation, and public-use proceedings. Targets how examiners and practitioners should prepare, document, and respond during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 to rebut inventorship/prior-art rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: When an article or patent discloses subject matter claimed in an application, the inventors named in the application must, if queried under subsection (f) or to rebut a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (e), provide a satisfactory showing by affidavit under 37 CFR 1.132 that the inventorship is correct and that the reference discloses subject matter derived from the applicant rather than invented by the author or patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An uncontradicted “unequivocal statement” from the applicant may be accepted to establish inventorship (In re DeBaun). However, such statements may be insufficient if there is evidence to the contrary (e.g., Ex parte Kroger). A successful 1.132 affidavit establishing derivation does not change the publication date of the reference for defeating later references (In re Costello). Examples show conversion from 102(a)/(e) prior art to non-prior-art under 102(b) if the applicant is shown to be the author/patentee originator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of attribution affidavit (does not antedate publication date)
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit or declaration establishing derivation by the author or patentee of a first reference does not enable an applicant to assume the author/patentee's publication date so as to defeat a later second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit establishes derivation for inventorship/prior art purposes but cannot be used to change the effective date of the first reference for purposes of other prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of identity of entities on prior-art status (Examples 1 & 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference fully describes the claimed invention and the applicant is the author/patentee and it was published/patented less than one year prior, the reference cannot be used against the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 102(b). If the author/patentee is a different entity, the reference is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the latter situation an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.132 may be submitted to show derivation and attempt to convert the fact situation to the former (i.e., make it fall within the 1-year grace).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130: disqualifying a commonly owned patent as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 in view of a U.S. patent that is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), and the inventions in the application/patent and the patent are not identical but not patentably distinct, and are owned by the same party, the patent may be disqualified as prior art by submission of (1) a terminal disclaimer under § 1.321(c), and (2) an oath or declaration stating current common ownership and that the inventor named in the application/patent is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.130(a) applies only in situations described (A)-(C). The oath/declaration may be signed by the inventor(s), attorney of record, or assignee(s) of the entire interest. The inventor named must have invented the claimed subject matter before the actual date of invention of the reference patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and interplay of 37 CFR 1.130 with other remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.130 is limited to overcoming rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on commonly owned U.S. patents and requires a terminal disclaimer; an applicant cannot use 37 CFR 1.131 to antedate a commonly owned patent, and interference practice is restricted when the patent is commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because an interference will not be declared or continued between an application and an unexpired patent owned by a single party, 1.130 fills the narrow remedial gap for commonly owned patents that are not prior art under 102(b) but give rise to 103 rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on dates for establishing 'prior inventor' under 35 U.S.C. 104
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase “prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104” requires that the inventor be the prior inventor within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 104, and an applicant or patent owner may not establish a date of invention in certain foreign countries before specified cutoff dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, an applicant may not: (A) establish a date in a foreign country other than a NAFTA or WTO member; (B) establish a date in a WTO member country other than a NAFTA country earlier than January 1, 1996; or (C) establish a date in a NAFTA country other than the U.S. earlier than December 8, 1993.

rubrics_metrics.name: File wrapper contents: what to enter and not enter on 'Contents'
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that do not become a permanent part of the record should not be entered on the 'Contents' of the file wrapper. All papers legally entered are given a paper number and should not be withdrawn or returned without special authority of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.59 permits return of certain accidentally-submitted documents or proprietary information not important to patentability decisions. Certain foreign-executed oaths may be returned but a copy retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of papers in the file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Until revision for allowance, specification, amendments and applicant communications are fastened to the left side (center fold) in inverse chronological order; Office actions and other Office communications fastened to right side, with drawing print always on top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When duplicates are submitted, duplicates are destroyed except in certain timing situations. At allowance, only papers required by the printer are placed in the left (center) section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and endorsement of drawing prints
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints of the drawing are fastened inside the file wrapper by the Office of Initial Patent Examination; white paper prints are kept on top. All prints and inked sketches subsequently filed to be part of the record should be endorsed with the application number of the corresponding application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 608.02(m) for endorsement practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to file wrapper data and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner notices an error in data on the file wrapper or PALM bib-data sheet, they should return the application to OIPE for correction or have technical support correct PALM data and print a new bib-data sheet for placement in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances requiring correction include: inventorship changes (37 CFR 1.48), filing date corrections, prior U.S. application number errors (see § 202.02), and priority claim corrections under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c). Applications sent to OIPE should be accompanied by an OIPE Data Base Routing Slip explaining the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name or residence changes: treatment and distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinction between 'residence' and Post Office address must be observed. Unless specifically requested by applicant, the residence will not be changed on the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 605.04(c) for procedures when applicant changes name; do not change residence entry absent request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification during examination: recording and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is received, the classification and the initials/name of the examiner assigned are noted in pencil in designated spaces on the file wrapper; these notations should be kept current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure classification and docket designation reflect current examiner assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of Claims maintenance and annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the 'Index of Claims' up to date as a reliable index of claims and amendments. Use preprinted claim numbers for original claims and an adjacent column for final numbering of allowed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent claims should be encircled in red ink. Draw red lines below numbers corresponding to original and subsequently added claims; annotate first claim of each amendment with the amendment letter. If claims are rewritten under 37 CFR 1.121(a), do not strike original claim number but note 'Amend. 1' (and update for subsequent rewrites). Cancelled claims should have a line drawn through their number. Examiner records date and type of each Office action and places final patent claim numbers at allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action search endorsement and search-update documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits, the examiner shall endorse in black ink the classes and subclasses (domestic and foreign patents, abstract collections, publications) in which the search was made and indicate the date(s) the search was conducted. In subsequent actions, the examiner must endorse that the search has been updated and identify additional fields searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search updates should include all databases and the search queries and classifications employed in the original search. Great care should be taken to clearly indicate places searched and dates. See MPEP § 904 for search procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEARCHED vs SEARCH NOTES: what to record where
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches are separated into two categories: entries to be recorded in the 'SEARCHED' box (which will be printed under 'Field of Search' on the patent front page except updates) and entries to be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box (not printed but important to the record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record a complete search of a subclass (including all U.S. and foreign patent documents) in 'SEARCHED' with full classification. Limited searches of a subclass (or publications-only searches) generally go in 'SEARCH NOTES' unless otherwise directed. Updates in 'SEARCHED' should be marked '(updated)'. Follow examples in MPEP for formatting (e.g., '424/270', '414/DIG.4 (updated)').

rubrics_metrics.name: SEARCH NOTES entries: cursory searches, consultations, literature searches, and parent refs
rubrics_metrics.description: Record cursory or scanning searches as '(cursory)'; consultations with other examiners as '(consulted)' (optionally with examiner name and art unit); searches of publications not in classified patent file with publication info (periodical, book, abstracting service) and period covered; and reviews of art cited in parent or related applications with notation 'refs. checked' and application or patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific examples provided (e.g., '250/13 (cursory)', 'Chem. Abs, Palladium hydride Jan.-June 1975', 'S. N. 495,123 refs. checked'). Note exceptions where references could not be checked and explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements for computer/database searches
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions involving a search of a computer-accessed text, chemical-structure, or sequence database, the examiner shall endorse in the SEARCH NOTES box: the search logic or chemical structure/sequence used as a query; the name of the file(s) searched and the database service; the date of the search; and the examiner's initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum documentation can be provided by (1) supplying and annotating the computer search printout, (2) recording the information on PTO-1590 Search Request Form, or (3) recording the required information in the SEARCH NOTES box. When using printouts, indicate which search statements' results were reviewed (circle them in black ink), hole-punch and place printouts in the file wrapper. See Table 1 for service-specific history/print behavior and missing elements that must be supplemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of search-history printouts and missing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some database services' history commands omit elements (e.g., database name, date). Missing elements must be documented by annotating the printout, including the log off command output, or writing the missing data on the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 lists history commands and missing elements per database service (STN, Dialog, Questel, WEST, etc.). For structure/sequence searches, include query sequence and beginning of result file and clearly relate query sequences to search results by annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording searches of other/publicly accessible databases and media
rubrics_metrics.description: For other publicly accessible computer-accessed databases (e.g., CD-ROMs, specialized databases), record sufficient identification of the material searched and sufficient search query information so the search can be updated, including location and form (e.g., CD-ROM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples for citation (e.g., 'Entrez: Sequences, NCBI, Version 7.19.91b (CD-ROM) Searched HIV and vaccine; ... on April 1, 1990').

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters not recorded on the file wrapper (IDS consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration or nonconsideration of prior art citations submitted by applicant in Information Disclosure Statements (37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98) is not recorded on the file wrapper; see MPEP § 609 for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use file-wrapper SEARCHED/SEARCH NOTES boxes to indicate whether IDS citations were considered; follow § 609 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.292 public use proceedings: petition threshold and hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition for institution of public use proceedings supported by affidavits/declarations makes a prima facie showing that an invention claimed was in public use or on sale more than one year before the filing date, a hearing may be had before the Commissioner to determine whether to institute public use proceedings. If instituted, testimony procedures under §§ 1.671–1.685 apply and the petitioner will be heard but will not be heard further in prosecution after decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(j), be served on the applicant in accordance with § 1.248 (or filed in duplicate if service impossible), and be submitted prior to mailing of a notice of allowance (§ 1.311). Duplicate copies should be submitted only when service is not possible despite diligent effort; bulky papers may be represented by a notice in the file with the papers available separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file public use petitions and ex parte vs inter partes distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.292 (private persons, corporations, government agencies). There are two types: ex parte (petitioner not entitled to inspect pending application) and inter partes (pending application is a reissue application and petitioner is privy to application contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner who was once involved in a terminated interference with a pending application is treated as an ex parte petitioner. Petitions filed on/after February 11, 1985 are limited unless they arise from interferences declared prior to that date or similar grandfathered circumstances. A petition by a party to an interference is generally not allowed for applications in interference (see § 1.292(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use petitions in restricted applications and effect on nonelected subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If a public use petition is filed in an application that has been restricted, and the petition alleges statutory-bar subject matter covering elected and nonelected claims, only the portion drawn to elected claims will be considered unless a proceeding is instituted; however, if proceedings are instituted, they may include nonelected subject matter and any evidence adduced on nonelected subject matter may be used in subsequently-filed applications without requiring a new fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner will not be heard regarding the appropriateness of a restriction requirement. Evidence from public use proceedings can affect later related applications.
